headline: French startup Tissium develops liquid polymer that helps nerves heal, now available to US surgeons
summary: A new biopolymer acts as a temporary splint, allowing severed peripheral nerves to mend with 100% success in trials, outperforming traditional sutures.
details: French firm Tissium has developed a thick, sticky liquid biopolymer designed to help peripheral nerves heal after injury. This innovative treatment is now available for surgeons to purchase in the US, offering a new approach to nerve repair.

The biopolymer, made of naturally occurring fatty acid and glycerol, attaches to tissue when exposed to light. It acts like an internal splint, holding nerve ends in place while the body naturally mends itself, then biodegrades once healing is complete.

Peripheral nerve injuries, often from cuts or machinery, can lead to loss of feeling or chronic pain if not properly aligned during healing. Traditional micro-sutures are a delicate technique, and Tissium aims to provide a less traumatic and more consistent method.

A US trial with 12 patients who suffered finger nerve injuries showed remarkable results: all 12 regained the ability to feel temperature, pain, texture, and light touch. This compares to a little over 80% success rate with other techniques, and no patients reported pain or device-related complications after a year.

Tissium has secured €30 million in private investments and €30 million in debt financing from the European Investment Bank. This funding will support commercialization and further research and development, with manufacturing continuing in northern France.

The company plans to expand its technology to other medical applications, including hernia treatment. A US trial is expected to enroll around 200 patients to test the biopolymer's ability to improve consistency and outcomes in hernia repair.

Early results from a European study on 78 hernia patients indicate that surgeons were able to apply Tissium's treatment 100% of the time. Patients showed improved quality of life, reduced pain, better recovery, and a lower recurrence rate of hernias.

Tissium is also developing products for cardiovascular reconstruction, an application conceived nearly 20 years ago. New funding will support a randomized pivotal trial in the US for its cardiovascular product, marking another significant step in its medical innovation journey.

headline_marked: [[ishvacerto proves AI code]] or finds exact breaking inputs, with 0 false alarms
headline: ishvacerto proves AI code or finds exact breaking inputs, with 0 false alarms
summary: ishvacerto is a new Python tool that verifies AI-generated code, providing exact failing inputs for bugs or abstaining if unsure. It guarantees zero false alarms on correct code, ensuring safe deployment.
details: AI coding assistants can ship confident bugs that only appear in production. ishvacerto acts as a gate, verifying generated code against doctests, your tests, or a reference implementation. It returns "VERIFIED", "REFUTED", or "ABSTAIN", never bluffing when it can't confirm.

The tool's power lies in its "REFUTED" output, which provides the exact failing input that breaks the code. This ensures developers get actionable insights without false alarms on correct code, making AI-generated code safer to ship.

On the HumanEval benchmark (164 problems), ishvacerto produced 0 false alarms on correct solutions. It captured a checkable doctest spec on 76 problems (approx. 46%) and abstained on the rest, even flagging a bug in HumanEval's own doctest.

Future plans include a reference proposer to retrieve verified references for code lacking tests, expanding coverage while maintaining zero false alarms. A differential mode generates inputs to find disagreements between candidate and reference implementations.

ishvacerto is pure Python, has zero dependencies, and is MIT licensed. It runs entirely on your machine, ensuring no telemetry, cloud interaction, or code leaving your box. A VS Code extension is also available for inline counterexample display.
